messages:
maria_sales: @here quick sync — FinServCo POC requires EU-only data residency (no US subprocessors allowed), BYO-KMS, and a deterministic routing policy. Need: list of supported EU regions, explicit subprocessor attestation, routing failover behavior, and POC pricing delta. Kickoff planned next Tue, deadline for answers COB Fri.

alex_sre: For EU-only we can pin tenants to eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 / eu-west-3. Subprocessors in-scope: cloud infra (AWS eu-central-1), storage (GCS eu-west-1/3), and monitoring (Datadog EU). We can produce an attestation PDF but legal will need ~3 business days. We can add tenant routing tags to enforce pinning. @jenna_se can confirm BYO-KMS ops.

jenna_se: Confirmed: BYO-KMS supported for Dedicated and Private. Customer must provide key ID/ARN + IAM service role or equivalent. We never import keys; we only hold an encryption envelope. Note: BYO-KMS triggers additional compliance review (approx 10 business days) for enterprise plans. I'll draft the runbook (IAM policy, required headers, sample curl).

mike_presales: Pricing quick note: geo-pin add-on is +15% on top of reserved commit pricing. Strict EU-only (no global failover) is +25% due to capacity reservation. For a 30-day POC we can propose a temporary waiver of the geo-pin fee if they move to Dedicated within 90 days — needs RevOps signoff. I'll prepare two quote variants.

oliver_ops: Ops caveat: pinning at the tenant level prevents cross-region overflow. We can provide a standby region in EU for failover inside the same continent; global fallback is possible but requires explicit customer consent and will be toggled off for strict EU-only. If they want control-plane entirely inside their VPC (no telemetry leaving customer network), escalate to @security.

security_bot: Automated report: potential risk items detected for strict EU requirement — third_party_monitoring (Datadog) operates EU endpoints but vendor support staff may access from non-EU IPs. Document link: https://intra.redwood/psubs/eu. Ticket opened SEC-2026-142 for subprocessor attestation and access controls.

maria_sales: Action items: 1) @alex_sre confirm final region list + latency/throughput profile, 2) @jenna_se produce BYO-KMS runbook and sample IAM trust, 3) @mike_presales share POC quote with waived-fee option, 4) @security (cc security_bot) run attestation & confirm Datadog access constraints. Need all artifacts by COB Fri.

alex_sre: Region list confirmed: eu-west-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-3. Attaching quick perf notes (token TPS estimates). Proposed routing policy (example snippet below) — prefer pinned region, standby in-continent, fallback global only with signed consent:
```
routing_policy: {
  "primary": "eu",
  "standby": "eu",
  "fallback": "global",
  "pinning": true,
  "consent_required": true
}
```

jenna_se: Draft runbook in progress. Will include sample curl to register customer KMS and an example IAM trust policy. Also adding checklist for Dedicated vs Hosted differences.

mike_presales: Sending the two-variant POC quote to this thread in ~2 hours. Will mark the waived-fee option as conditional on Dedicated conversion.

security_bot: SEC-2026-142 updated: requested vendor attestation (Datadog) and confirmation of EU-only support for monitoring access. Expected turnaround 4 business days.

maria_sales: Perfect — thanks team. Drop docs here when ready and I'll loop FinServCo. :thumbsup:
